## Capturing a clean round

Codex stores Responses API items rather than Claude transcript records.
Clikernel activity appears as native custom `exec` calls whose logical
operation is `tools.mcp__clikernel__execute`. A capture isolates one
successful active round, removes reasoning and host polling noise, and
regenerates stable ids.

### Deferred host calls

A slow terminal interaction may be recorded as an initial
`custom_tool_call_output`, followed by a host-level `wait` function call
carrying the real result.
[`collapse_deferred`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/codexdojo.html#collapse_deferred)
restores the simpler logical call/result pair that belongs in a worked
example.

### collapse_deferred

``` python
def collapse_deferred(
    src
):
```

*Custom call/result pairs, replacing host-level deferred waits with
their final result*

``` python
c = codex_custom_call('tools.mcp__clikernel__execute', dict(code='1+1'), 'call_c')
test_eq(_cell(c), '1+1')
direct = [c,codex_custom_output('call_c','2')]
test_eq(collapse_deferred(direct), direct)
test_eq(collapse_deferred([*direct,c]),direct)
wait = codex_call('wait', dict(cell_id='9'), 'call_w')
deferred = [c,codex_custom_output('call_c','Script running with cell ID 9'),wait,codex_output('call_w','2')]
back = collapse_deferred(deferred)
test_eq(_out_text(back[1]), '2')
test_eq(back[1]['call_id'], 'call_c')
```

selects native custom calls by logical tool name and either an argument

handles long cells without copying their whole source into the curation

### Capturing from a live session

[`capture_current`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_current)
remains useful when a clean round has already happened in an interactive
Codex thread. It keeps the contiguous native custom-call pairs from the
first bootstrap `doc(clik, pysk, edsk)` call through the first clean
score. Host-required skill reads before that call remain live session
context rather than becoming stale template content.

The capture is gated before it is converted into the review dialog. A
supplied `docs` list can override the documented-tool metadata;
otherwise
[`capture_current`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_current)
derives it from the captured standalone `doc(...)` cells, so MCP worker
identity does not affect the stored template.

## Template dialog

A live capture can be curated without replaying the whole thread.
[`pick_turns`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/codexdojo.html#pick_turns)
selects clikernel code exactly, falling back to prefix matching, while
[`pick_calls`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/codexdojo.html#pick_calls)
can select any supported nested tool by name and arguments.

### Building the review dialog

[`mk_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#mk_template)
adds the synthetic user prompt and short framing messages around already
selected native tool pairs. Disabling tool truncation preserves every
receipt byte-for-byte for rebuilding.

<a

*A template dialog with native tool output left untruncated*

``` python

test_eq(tdlg.meta, dict(llmdojo=dict(doced=['doc','rg'])))
test_eq(tdlg.messages[0].content, TMPL_PROMPT)
```

The packaged dialog and store must agree, since the store is compiled
from the dialog. Read that reviewed artifact through the same conversion
path and reject it if its calls, score, or completion receipt no longer
survive the round trip.

``` python
packaged = read_ipynb(str(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb'))
packaged_items = dlg2items(packaged)
assert dojo_cid(packaged_items)
test_eq(is_clean(packaged_items), [])
```

## Template store

The store keeps native Responses items plus the clean-round completion
id, dojo version, and documented-tool state. It is package data,
compiled from the canonical dialog by `dojobuild` and shipped with the
code, so updating llmdojo updates the template with nothing per-user to
rebuild.

[`save_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#save_template)
writes native items and the metadata needed to replay them: completion
id, dojo version, and documented-tool state.

## Launching

Creating a dojo session starts a Codex thread, injects the native
template, registers its completion receipt, and seeds the
documented-tool state. Appending performs the same injection at the tail
of an existing thread after compaction.

### Starting a thread

[`prep_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#prep_dojo)
creates a persisted Codex thread, injects a freshly re-id’d copy of the
template, registers its completion, and seeds the matching documentation
receipts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llmdojo/blob/main/llmdojo/claudedojo.py#L187"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### prep_dojo

``` python
async def prep_dojo(
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project to start in; current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    codex_home:NoneType=None, # Alternate Codex home, primarily for tests
):
```

*Create a thread containing the template and return its id*

### Refreshing after compaction

[`append_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#append_dojo)
appends a fresh copy of the worked round to an existing thread and
changes only its synthetic prompt to explain why the exercise is
repeating.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llmdojo/blob/main/llmdojo/claudedojo.py#L198"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### append_dojo

``` python
async def append_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Thread id to append to; newest thread for the project if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    codex_home:NoneType=None, # Alternate Codex home
):
```

*Append the template to an existing thread and return its id*

[`append_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#append_dojo)
is the post-compaction repair. Native compaction replaces the worked
history with a summary, so appending restores the demonstrations at the
tail and merges their documented-tool state. Re-salting ids makes
repeated repairs safe.

``` python
# App-server integration: isolated CODEX_HOME, no model turn.
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    home,proj = Path(td),Path(td)/'project'
    proj.mkdir()
    sid = await prep_dojo(proj,store,home)
    back = thread2dlg(sid,home,mx=None)
    assert any(m.msg_type=='prompt' and m.content==TMPL_PROMPT for m in back.messages)
    test_eq(is_clean(active_items(load_rollout(sid,home))),[])
    test_eq(json.loads((_state_root()/'doced'/f'{sid}.json').read_text()),['doc','rg'])
```

### Compacting with the DSL

Native Codex compaction is encrypted and needs a model turn;
[`llmsurgery.oai.compact_session`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmsurgery/oai.html#compact_session)
instead writes a readable compact-DSL document straight into the
rollout, offline.
[`compact_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#compact_dojo)
chains the two steps — dsl-compact the thread with earlier rounds
stripped out of the document, then append a fresh round — so
`codexdojo -c` resumes a session that is both short and re-demonstrated.

The DSL compact should carry the conversation’s work, not its warm-up:
the fresh round appended afterwards supersedes any earlier one. As on
the Claude side, a round occupies whole user turns, so
[`strip_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#strip_dojo)
chunks the items with the shared
[`_turns`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/tmpl.html#_turns) and
drops the turns that dealt a round; `compact_session`’s `strip` hook
applies it before anything is compacted. A thread holding nothing but
rounds is compacted whole rather than emptied.

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llmdojo/blob/main/llmdojo/claudedojo.py#L218"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### compact_dojo

``` python
async def compact_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Thread id to compact; newest thread for the project if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    codex_home:NoneType=None, # Alternate Codex home
):
```

*Synthetically compact a thread with the compact DSL (previous dojo
rounds removed first), then append the template round; returns its id*

``` python
# App-server integration: isolated CODEX_HOME, no model turn.
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    home,proj = Path(td),Path(td)/'project'
    proj.mkdir()
    sid = await prep_dojo(proj,store,home)
    work = custom_turn('What season is it?','tools.mcp__clikernel__execute',dict(code='season()'),'winter','Winter.')
    async with codex_client(home) as codex: await codex.append_thread(sid,work)
    test_eq(await compact_dojo(sid,proj,store,home), sid)
    prior,new = split_compaction(load_rollout(sid,home))
    body = item_txt(prior[-1])
    assert 'dojo_start()' not in body
    test('season()', body, in_)
    assert any(item_txt(o)==APPEND_PROMPT for o in new)   # codex records fresh context items at resume, ahead of the injected round
    test_eq(is_clean(active_items(load_rollout(sid,home))),[])
```

### Command line

A `call_parse` CLI mirroring `claudedojo`’s (the capitalized params
declare the short flags: `Resume` → `-r`, `Compact` → `-c`): every mode
prepares a thread and then execs `codex resume` on it, with standing
arguments from `launch_config('codex')` (the `codex_args` list in
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/codexdojo/config.toml`) and anything the launcher
doesn’t recognize forwarded via `nested=True`. The id comes right after
`resume`, so a stray forwarded token lands in codex’s optional prompt
slot rather than stealing the session id; forwarded flag values still
need `--flag=value` form, and the fresh-launch path rejects a stray
`sess` loudly. `--sid` prints the prepared id and exits. Store builds
live in `dojobuild`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llmdojo/blob/main/llmdojo/claudedojo.py#L239"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### main

``` python
def main(
    sess:str=None, # Thread id; the project's newest where omitted
    Resume:bool=False, # Append the round to an existing thread after compaction, then resume it
    Compact:bool=False, # Synthetically compact the thread with the compact DSL, then append the round and resume
    sid:bool=False, # Print the prepared thread id instead of launching codex
    capture:bool=False, # Run a clean round in a bare Codex child and store it
    current:bool=False, # Store the clean round an existing thread already played (`capture_current`)
):
```

*Prepare a Codex thread opening with the worked round and launch
`codex resume` on it; template maintenance is `dojobuild`*

## Rebuilding

Run `codexdojo --capture` to start a clean dojo round in a separate
scratch project and write the accepted round to the local template
store. The command uses the same packaged capture prompt as Claude,
delivered through the scratch project’s `AGENTS.md`. It also writes
`template.ipynb` beside the store for review. Curate that dialog with
`reply2dlg` and `dlg2reply`, then rebuild the stores with
`dojobuild --codex` (and `--claude`). Use `--current` when the source
thread already completed a clean round.
